### Diagnosis

The failing test `testMapValueEquality` in `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.JXPath151Test` is testing the comparison of values in a map using the XPath expression `map/b != map/a`. The current bug report mentions that comparing a value to `null` using unequals (`!=`) yields false in some cases. This could suggest an issue with handling `null` values in comparisons.

By looking at the `assertXPathValue` method in `org.apache.commons.jxpath.JXPathTestCase`, we can see that the method sets the context to be non-lenient and then retrieves the value of the given XPath expression to compare it with the expected value using `assertEquals`.

Since the failing test specifically compares values in a map where one value is `null`, it is possible that the comparison logic in the JXPath library does not handle `null` values correctly, leading to unexpected results in comparisons involving `null`.

### Hypothesis

There may be an issue in the JXPath library where comparisons involving `null` values do not behave as expected, potentially yielding incorrect results.

### Suggestions for Fixing
- `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.JXPathContext.getObject(JXPathContext, Pointer)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
